reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E equipped with its Borel measurable structure, every joint probability measure P on E times R such that P.map Prod.fst equals the actual centered identity-covariance standard Gaussian on E, every real polynomial p, and a supplied witness of MemLp(z->z.2,2,P) for the actual response coordinate, use these definitions. Let U={w:E | norm(w)=1}, with its inherited subspace topology and Borel measurable structure. For every rho:Measure U and x:E define predictor(rho,x)=integral_U p.eval(inner_product(w,x)) drho(w). Define risk(rho)=integral_{E times R}(predictor(rho,z.1)-z.2)^2 dP(z), and potential(rho,w)=2*integral_{E times R}(predictor(rho,z.1)-z.2)*p.eval(inner_product(w,z.1)) dP(z). All integrals are the actual real Bochner integrals on the whole indicated spaces, syntactically totalized when genuine integrability is absent. For any subsequently quantified pair rho0,rho1 define curve(t)=ofReal(1-t) times rho0 + ofReal(t) times rho1 for t:R, using literal positive-measure scaling and addition and ofReal(r)=max(r,0) embedded in the nonnegative extended reals. Abbreviate D=integral_U potential(rho0,w) drho1(w)-integral_U potential(rho0,w) drho0(w). The conclusion is the conjunction of the following two universal statements. First: For every probability rho on U, the actual squared joint residual z->(predictor(rho,z.1)-z.2)^2 is genuinely Bochner integrable under P, and for every w in U the scalar cross term z->(predictor(rho,z.1)-z.2)*p.eval(inner_product(w,z.1)) is genuinely Bochner integrable under P. Second: For every rho0,rho1:Measure U which are both probability measures, potential(rho0,.) is genuinely Bochner integrable under rho0 and under rho1; the real function t->risk(curve(t)) has derivative D within the closed interval [0,1] at endpoint 0, using its actual value at 0; and risk(rho0)+D<=risk(rho1). The only supplied analytic moment premise is L2 membership of the actual response, meaning almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm under the joint law. No independent feature-integrability or residual-integrability premise is given; the displayed joint and parameter integrability statements are generated conclusions. Parameter probability laws are arbitrary, including nonatomic laws, and the first statement quantifies every unit w regardless of where rho is supported. It therefore certifies the inner potential integrals genuinely for all unit directions when rho is a probability, rather than just at its atoms. P is a true joint law: its actual first-coordinate pushforward is Gaussian, but no product decomposition or independence of the response and input is assumed. Every response in the formulas is the actual z.2. The same potential based at rho0 is integrated under rho1 and rho0; their real difference has new-minus-base direction and is never positive or truncated subtraction of measures. The loss is unhalved, so potential has literal factor 2. On [0,1] the curve is the actual convex probability mixture, with curve(0)=rho0 and curve(1)=rho1. The endpoint derivative is right-sided relative to that closed interval and includes risk(curve(0))=risk(rho0). Outside [0,1] the displayed formula uses clipped nonnegative coefficients, so the conclusion is not an unrestricted derivative of that outside extension. The support inequality compares the two actual risks using exactly the same scalar difference as the derivative; D need not be nonnegative. No finite-support, particle-count, uniform norm-budget, or positive-degree assumption is imposed. The statement asserts these segment derivatives and support inequalities for all probability pairs, without specifying an ambient topology or a Frechet derivative on a space of signed measures. No positive dimension is required; in zero dimension U is empty and the probability-law implications have no laws satisfying their premises. The zero polynomial is allowed and gives zero predictors and potential and equality in the supporting inequality.
